problems.stem: Why do gecko-inspired adhesives often grip strongly in shear but release more easily during peeling?
options: Because adhesion disappears whenever the surface is tilted
Because the microstructures are oriented to create direction-dependent contact behavior
Because the adhesive works only on wet surfaces
Because van der Waals forces act only during vertical loading
problems.explanation: Directional microstructures create different contact mechanics depending on how the load is applied.

problems.stem: How do gecko setae make weak intermolecular forces useful at the macro scale?
options: By replacing van der Waals forces with magnetic attraction
By dramatically increasing effective contact area through many fine structures
By using liquid glue stored inside each seta
problems.explanation: Each contact is tiny, but many micro-contacts together create meaningful adhesion.

problems.stem: Which design goal is most aligned with gecko-inspired dry adhesives?
options: Single-use permanent bonding in structural concrete
Maximum stickiness regardless of contamination or surface roughness
Eliminating all dependence on surface geometry
problems.explanation: Dry adhesives are especially valuable when reversible, residue-free attachment is needed.

problems.stem: A team wants better reversible adhesion on a robot gripper. Which variable should they most likely adjust first?
options: Only the color of the pad
The geometry and orientation of micro-scale contact features
The battery voltage of the robot arm
The length of the user manual
problems.explanation: For biomimetic dry adhesion, contact geometry strongly shapes how load, release, and surface conformity behave.
